- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 1–2% for 30-day horizons.
- After a price spike, model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect — apply a dampening factor (e.g., 0.95) to subsequent forecast values to avoid excessive downward drift.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits strong mean-reversion bias — adjust forecasts to align with recent 5–7 day moving average rather than long-term trend.
- Forecast errors cluster near the end of the 30-day horizon — particularly days 25–30 — suggest model underestimates downward momentum; apply a slight upward bias (e.g., +0.5–1.0) to final 5–7 days if sentiment remains flat.
- If model forecast is >90% of recent 18-day high, reduce forecast by 2–3% to avoid overconfidence in upward momentum.
- If sentiment history is all 0.00, avoid using sentiment-based adjustments — treat as “neutral market” and rely on pure technical reversion logic.
